headline: FIREFLY GREEN BAY DRILLS 42m @ 6.1% CuEq — 50Mt Copper-Gold Project Gets PEA in August; FFM Added to S&P/ASX 200 (TSX/ASX: FFM)
snippet: FireFly Metals (TSX/ASX: FFM) published another standout quarter on July 27, with multi-rig underground drilling at Green Bay in Newfoundland delivering 42.0m at 6.1% CuEq — including 9.8m at 16.5% CuEq in a VMS zone — and 51.5m at 4.9% CuEq, against a resource of 50.4Mt at 2.0% CuEq M&I plus 29.3Mt at 2.5% CuEq Inferred. A PEA and scoping study for an upscaled production restart is on track for August 2026; simultaneously, FireFly was added to the S&P/ASX 200 Index, signalling that the project has reached institutional scale while much of the production optionality remains unpriced.

headline: HOT CHILI'S LA VERDE DELIVERS 250m @ 0.50% CuEq FROM 64m DEPTH — Near-Surface Porphyry Now Cornerstone of Costa Fuego (ASX/TSXV: HCH)
snippet: Hot Chili (ASX: HCH / TSXV: HCH) announced July 28 that RC drilling at the La Verde Cu-Au porphyry discovery in Chile returned 250m at 0.50% CuEq from 64m depth, including 36m at 0.72% CuEq — delineating a substantial near-surface enrichment zone located 30km south of the company's Costa Fuego copper-gold central processing hub. The consistency and shallow grade profile is elevating La Verde from a district growth option to a potential high-grade starter pit, ahead of a planned maiden mineral resource estimate that will be the first quantified measure of this discovery's size.

headline: SANTACRUZ SILVER Q2 2026: 1.57M oz Ag AND 23,240t Zn AS BOLIVAR MINE BOUNCES 32% QUARTER-ON-QUARTER (TSXV: SCZ)
snippet: Santacruz Silver Mining (TSXV: SCZ) reported Q2 2026 silver production of 1,573,100 oz — up 11% year-over-year — alongside 23,240 tonnes of zinc (+10% YoY) and lead up 18%, with the Bolivar mine in Bolivia rebounding 32% quarter-on-quarter as rehabilitation from May 2025 flooding continued. San Lucas processed 22% more ore than the prior quarter; across the multi-mine portfolio, nine percent higher consolidated tonnes milled drove gains across every payable metal, indicating that the company's base throughput recovery is now firmly in motion.

headline: SILVER AT $57.55 WITH GOLD-SILVER RATIO AT 70:1 — Sixth Straight Supply Deficit (46.3 Moz) Collides With Pre-FOMC Caution
snippet: Silver edged lower to $57.55 per ounce on July 28 as FOMC uncertainty and a firm U.S. dollar pressured the metal, widening the gold-silver ratio to approximately 70:1 — well above the long-run average of 60:1 and near extremes that have historically preceded sharp silver outperformance. The Silver Institute projects a sixth consecutive annual supply deficit of 46.3 million ounces in 2026; if Chair Warsh signals a hold-and-done posture Wednesday, the combination of structural shortage and an overstretched ratio sets up a historically compelling reversal trade heading into Q3.

headline: CITI HOLDS $15,000/t COPPER YEAR-END TARGET — Yangshan Import Premium Triples to $119/t; Chile Supply Risk Underpins Bull Case
snippet: Citi maintained its zero-to-three-month copper price target at $14,500 per metric tonne and its year-end target at $15,000/t on July 28, arguing that supply — not demand — is the more urgent variable: the Yangshan copper import premium has surged from $45/t at the start of 2026 to approximately $115–119/t, reflecting intensifying Chinese competition for overseas refined metal. LME copper dipped to $13,770/t on FOMC jitters, but Citi notes Chilean mine supply risks, a soft scrap market response to elevated prices, and declining ex-U.S. visible inventories as structural supports that central bank rate policy cannot neutralise.

headline: 8-FOR-8: NORTH AMERICAN NIOBIUM HITS REE PEGMATITE IN EVERY BARDY HOLE — 1,554m Done; Allanite (Nd, Pr) Assays Pending (CSE: NIOB)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / North American Niobium
snippet: North American Niobium (CSE: NIOB) completed its 2026 Bardy drill program in Quebec's Grenville Province on July 28, with all eight holes over 1,554 metres intersecting targeted syenitic pegmatite dykes — and core logging identifying coarse allanite (a rare-earth silicate hosting neodymium and praseodymium, both critical to permanent magnets) up to 2 cm wide in multiple intervals. Assays are pending; a further approximately 10,000-metre program across five Quebec properties is planned for the balance of 2026, incrementally derisking what may be a significant REE corridor in a politically stable, infrastructure-rich jurisdiction.

headline: NATIONS ROYALTY FISCAL 2026: REVENUE UP 91% TO C$1.61M — Cambria Red Mountain Gold Access Road Now Under Construction (TSXV: NRC)
snippet: Nations Royalty Corp. (TSXV: NRC) reported fiscal year-end results on July 28 showing royalty revenue up 91% year-over-year to C$1.61 million with C$17.1 million in cash — a strong balance sheet for a micro-cap royalty vehicle still early in its compounding phase. The standout portfolio development is Cambria Gold Mines commencing access road construction to the high-grade Red Mountain Gold Deposit in northwestern British Columbia on June 1, 2026 — the first concrete physical step toward a production decision that would convert Nations' royalty from a paper asset into recurring revenue.

headline: KITCO SWOT: SILVER LEADS ALL METALS AT +3.73% — DPM AND DISCOVERY SILVER BOTH UP 10%+ THIS WEEK; ETF Inflows Hit 1.09M oz
snippet: Kitco News' weekly Gold SWOT for July 27 highlighted silver as the best-performing precious metal for the week at +3.73%, with silver ETFs absorbing a net 1.09 million troy ounces in the latest session — a level of institutional accumulation that goes beyond tactical trading. Both DPM Metals and Discovery Silver (TSX: DSV) gained more than 10% over the week; the SWOT also flagged silver's increasingly structural role as a dual safe-haven and clean-energy industrial input, with platinum as the period's laggard — a reminder that not all precious metals are moving in lockstep as macro uncertainty bifurcates the group.

headline: TACTICAL RESOURCES CLOSES NASDAQ SPAC TODAY AS 'TREO' — U.S. Rare Earth Tailings Play Graduates From TSXV; Peak Texas Project Now Public
source_name: The Globe and Mail / Tactical Resources
snippet: Tactical Resources Corp. received Nasdaq approval and targeted July 28 as the closing date for its SPAC combination with Plum Acquisition Corp. III, listing the resulting issuer under the ticker TREO on the Nasdaq Capital Market — simultaneously delisting from the TSX Venture Exchange. The company's Peak rare earth project in Hudspeth County, Texas, takes a feedstock-first approach — processing already-extracted rare earth tailings rather than building a new mine — aiming to accelerate U.S. domestic rare earth supply capacity without the permitting timeline of a greenfield operation.
